paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is a God who does new things, and He does them for His people. He says, "Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it?" (Isaiah 43:19) I spent years in the back of a junk drawer thinking my story was done, so a promise like that hits me right in the apron. Whatever dry place you're standing in today, this is the God who says He will make "a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert." (Isaiah 43:19)

Now look at who gets that promise. These are the same people the LORD says have not called on Him and have burdened Him with their sins (Isaiah 43:22, 24). And still He says, "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake and remembers your sins no more." (Isaiah 43:25) Friend, that's not a little smudge cleaned off the counter. That's the whole mess wiped away, and He says He does it for His own sake.

But the passage doesn't end soft. It closes with hard words about destruction and reproach (Isaiah 43:28), and I think that's a heavy place to land. So I hold both: His mercy is real, and His words are serious. The LORD invites His people, "Remind Me, let us argue the matter together." (Isaiah 43:26) So bring Him all of it, baker, because He is your Redeemer, and He's the One who forgives.
